newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: ANC wants independent probe on S. African oil row.
newsitem.headline: ANC wants independent probe on S. African oil row.

text.p: The ruling African National Congress (ANC) said on Tuesday it was still determined to draw the Public Protector into the public row between South African Minerals and Energy Minister Penuell Maduna and Auditor-General Henri Kleuver.

Its parliamentary motion on the row, over alleged irregularities in the Strategic Fuel Fund (SFF) and Maduna's criticism of Kleuver, had fallen away earlier when the oppostion National Party withdrew its original motion.
But ANC chief whip Max Sisulu said he still wanted parliament to establish "parallel independent inquiries" into the row.

"It is our view that the Public Protector should be asked to investigate the Auditor General's reports on the SFF Association and that an all-party parliamentary committee should be asked to examine whether Maduna's actions were appropriate," he said.
"The ANC believes that a thorough public and impartial investigation of the facts of these issues is essential.

"The public has the right to know and our proposal will ensure that any of these investigations will be open and fair, free from prejudice, free from political interference and free from uninformed speculation."

The National Party withdrew its motion following the release of a resolution by the powerful audit commission on Monday which said it expected the parliamentary public accounts committee to examine the allegations and counter-allegations as part of its normal review of the work of the Auditor-General.
The commission, a statutory body which oversees the work of the Auditor-General, said that it planned to ask President Nelson Mandela to help end exchanges between the two in the media.
"(This is) damaging to the important principle of support and assistance between the various organs and institutions of state," it said.
